decision: Approve this exact consumer tuple for source admission. Release testing and live acceptance remain separate gates.

findings.topic: Diagnostic modules outside the Panic hash gate
findings.evidence: tests/unit/test_panic_dispatch_dependencies.py pins both sha256 values (match recomputed hashes) and checks helper.py imports both and keeps '@recorded_payload' on handle_payload. Mutation check in a scratch copy: appending one byte to either module, or removing the decorator, each fails exactly one test.
findings.judgement: Acceptable substitute. Extending PANIC_SOURCE_FILES would break admission of every older bundle and rollback target. The pin is a CI-time control, not runtime admission, so it relies on the existing rule that only CI-green signed releases ship. It is stricter than the pre-existing state of helper.py's other transitive imports (engine, config), which are also outside the gate (pre-existing, out of scope). Both modules import only the stdlib plus each other. Bypassing the decorator check requires editing helper.py, which is itself hash-gated.

findings.topic: Status-read waiters could fill the 8 helper slots
findings.evidence: helper.py:474-481. Lock tried non-blocking first; only on failure a non-blocking BoundedSemaphore(3) permit is taken, the timed wait (0.5 s) runs inside try/finally that always releases the permit (covers success, timeout and exceptions). Permit release only follows a successful acquire, so BoundedSemaphore cannot over-release and cannot leak. Waiter that obtains the lock gives up its permit, so at most 1 holder + 3 waiters = 4 of 8 slots. Access writes (operation != status) keep acquire(blocking=False). normal-access and reset never touch _access_lock or the semaphore (grep). dashboard-access is not served on the policy_only socket (2 slots), so the cap does not interact with it. Test test_waiting_status_reads_never_take_the_slots_panic_and_reset_need passes and checks budget recovery.
findings.residual: Other non-access actions (Wi-Fi/router actions, write waiters up to 3 s) can still occupy slots; that is pre-existing and not made worse.

findings.topic: Rollback removed journal settings while services were stopped
findings.evidence: updates.py:4132-4141 wait_restarted_healthy runs wait_healthy first, then configure_outage_journal remove only when the restored code lacks journal_policy.py. All four restart paths use it: restart_only retry (4177-4178), rollback (4245-4246 via restore() which ends in restart_services), exception rollback (4384-4385), exception stopped-restart (4387-4388). restart_services no longer calls it. Forward install path (4340-4343) is unchanged: health first, then install. No path missed.
findings.double_run: Possible but harmless: a failed rollback health check raises into the except branch which restores and runs the step again; and a restart_only retry followed by a later failure. The remove action is idempotent and bounded (10 s).
findings.failure: configure_outage_journal swallows OSError, ValueError and plain UpdateError and returns False, and healthy is returned regardless, so an ordinary failure cannot turn a successful rollback into a failed one. Only CommandNotStopped/OperationOwnershipUnknown propagate (deliberate existing gate); then the services are already restarted and healthy, the request is kept with command_pending and reported failed. This is conservative and strictly better than before F3, where the same exception left services stopped.

findings.topic: Nothing on the Panic path blocks
findings.evidence: recorded_payload wraps only listed actions; Operation/_emit/send_fields use a non-blocking module gate and a non-blocking AF_UNIX datagram send; all exceptions swallowed; the wrapped function's return and exceptions are unchanged. JournalHandler.handle bypasses the handler lock.

findings.topic: No secrets in records, exports or errors
findings.evidence: Records carry a fixed schema (format, operation id, source, action, phase, outcome, elapsed_ms, configuration_version) with no payload data. SafeFormatter allows only audited fixed templates and replaces every non-numeric argument with '[detail omitted]'. SafeServerErrors suppresses socketserver tracebacks and client addresses; sys/threading excepthooks log a fixed message.
Only diff: import and one configure_logging() call at main() start (logging setup and excepthooks).

journal_policy.py fixed SystemMaxUse=64M, SystemMaxFileSize=8M, MaxRetentionSec=7day, RuntimeMaxUse=8M; option allow-list; configure_outage_journal is best-effort and never fails the install path except for the pre-existing unknown-command gate.

No new lock is held across another lock; the waiter semaphore is only taken non-blocking and released before the access lock body runs; diagnostic gate is leaf and non-blocking. panic_guard.py byte-identical to the admitted bundles.
